topics.topic: Identity or generation mechanism that invalidates an import confirmation after re-upload
questions: How can Registry distinguish a replacement upload of identical bytes from the file to which the still-pending confirmation was bound?

What state invalidates the pending confirmation when a successful re-upload has the same bytes and therefore the same digest: does upload clear it, or is an upload identity or generation retained and bound to it?

judgement.why: This is the same identical-re-upload question as P1; the added security-review coverage statement changes no operational rule, and the passages that P1 relied on remain unchanged.

precedent.topic: Whether an identical re-upload invalidates pending import confirmation and how to distinguish upload instances
quotes:
The uploaded file is kept in the owner session that uploaded it, in the
   process's memory only — never in the store, never on a disk — until the import is accepted, another file is uploaded in that
   session — one of the same bytes included — or the session ends (M11); then it is dropped.

Confirming a mapping after another file was uploaded in the session is
   refused: the file it named is no longer kept — also when the new file has
   the same bytes.
precedent.why: The texts expressly treat every later upload, identical bytes included, as replacing the earlier file and require the earlier confirmation to be refused; the internal mechanism used to enforce that outcome does not change observable behaviour.

topics.topic: Semantics of create requests replayed after anonymisation or customer erasure
questions: Does a replay after the original project was anonymised or Customer erased create a second record, or does the primary-action prohibition still apply?
Is the post-erasure request treated as an ordinary new create that may fail current validation, or must it always create and return a record as the changed passages say?

quotes: missing name, or an object without an address, refused (R0-45); a customer reference that is unknown, erased, restricted or ended refused (R0-16, R0-51, R0-57); a retried create never makes a second project (R0-36)

A request id leaves its record with the values anonymisation or erasure
   removes (M01, M04); a create arriving after that with the same request id
   is a new create, answered with the new record it made, so it is not silent
   (R0-36, owner, 2026-11-01).
judgement.divergence: One passage refuses the replay or prohibits a second project; the other creates and returns a new project, which the owner observes.
judgement.why: The unqualified primary-action rule conflicts with the later exception that expressly makes and returns a new record after anonymisation or erasure.

bases.passage: missing name, or an object without an address, refused (R0-45); a customer reference that is unknown, erased, restricted or ended refused (R0-16, R0-51, R0-57); a retried create never makes a second project (R0-36)
bases.rests_on:
A create repeated after a lost answer — with or without a caller-supplied id —
never silently makes a second project, customer or room, and never damages one.
The mechanism belongs to State 2.

bases.passage:
A request id leaves its record with the values anonymisation or erasure
   removes (M01, M04); a create arriving after that with the same request id
   is a new create, answered with the new record it made, so it is not silent
   (R0-36, owner, 2026-11-01).
bases.rests_on:
This holds while the record the first create made keeps its values (owner,
2026-11-01). Erasing a customer or anonymising a project removes everything
that would tell a repeat (R0-06, R0-62); a create repeated after that is a new
create, and its answer shows the new record it made.

witness.initial: Project P was created by the owner with request id K while naming usable Customer C; P is now archived and anonymised, and C is now restricted.
events: The owner resubmits the original create-project request with request id K, the original facts and Customer C.
outcomes: The primary-action passage refuses the request because C is restricted and, independently, says a retried create never makes a second project.
A01 rule 8 treats K as a new create and says its answer contains the new project it made.
witness.observer: The owner, who sees either a refusal with no new identity or a newly created project.
basis:
The acting principal of a creation or a correction is the owner, always
(Primary actions): the project keeps no "created by".

When the owner anonymises or deletes an archived project, it leaves the granted
set of every agent session, and a session whose active project it was has none.

A project may name no customer. When it names one, at creation or correction,
that Customer exists and is not erased; a project whose customer is erased
later keeps naming it (R0-06).

topics.topic: Serialization and permitted outcomes when create replay races anonymisation or erasure
questions: What outcomes are permitted when a replay using request id K races the transaction that removes K from the original record, and must both operations be serialised against the same request-id lookup?

When a create using an existing request id runs concurrently with anonymising its Project or erasing its Customer, which operation is considered first, and must both operations be linearized under one lock or transaction boundary?

quotes:
A request id is looked up among the records of the same model — for 'add a
   room' and 'publish an artifact pointer', only those of the project the
   call names, so a record of another project is never reached through it.
   A create whose request id such a record carries is
   a repeat when the facts it supplies equal that record's current facts of
   the same kind: Registry answers the record as it stands now and changes
   nothing. A publish's repeat answers the pointer whatever its status now; it
   neither supersedes nor makes a version (R0-17, R0-88).

Creates of one model carrying
   one request id are applied one at a time: of two concurrent ones, the
   first makes the record and the second is a repeat or refused by rule 4
   or 5.

A request id leaves its record with the values anonymisation or erasure
   removes (M01, M04); a create arriving after that with the same request id
   is a new create, answered with the new record it made, so it is not silent
   (R0-36, owner, 2026-11-01).
Every action is atomic: it applies all its changes or none.

Several
   owner sessions may be open at once; signing in ends none of the others.
judgement.divergence: One implementation linearizes the replay before anonymisation, returning the existing archived project and creating nothing; another linearizes anonymisation first, then creates and returns a new active project. The owner observes the different identity, response and catalogue.
judgement.why: The texts serialize creates with other creates and make each action atomic, but do not order or serialize a request-id lookup against the anonymisation or erasure that removes that request id.

witness.initial: Archived Project P carries request id K and the facts F of its original create; two valid owner sessions are open.
events: Through one owner session, the owner confirms anonymisation of P.
Concurrently through the other owner session, the owner resubmits the original create request with request id K and facts F.
outcomes: The replay is applied first, finds K and returns P unchanged; anonymisation then removes K, and no new project is created.
Anonymisation is applied first and removes K; the replay then finds no matching record and creates and returns a new active project.
witness.observer: The owner, who receives either the archived original identity or a new active identity and later sees a different project catalogue.

   owner sessions may be open at once; signing in ends none of the others.
